hero.subtitle:
Own a real farming plot outside Yerevan.
A farmer tends it for you.
Harvest comes to your door weekly.

problem.heading: You have no idea what you're actually eating.

cards.title: You don't know where it came from
cards.description: Most produce travels hundreds of kilometers. By the time it reaches you, it's been in cold storage for weeks.

cards.title: Pesticides you can't taste or see
cards.description: Conventional farming uses chemical inputs you can't detect. There's no way to know what's on your food.

cards.title: Picked before it was ready
cards.description: Produce is harvested early to survive transit. You're eating food that never had the chance to fully ripen.

howItWorks.heading: Four steps to your own plot.
howItWorks.intro: No farming experience needed. We handle everything from soil to your door.

steps.title: Choose your plot & crop
steps.description: Browse plots in Armenian farming regions. Pick your preferred size, what grows on it — tomatoes, cucumbers, herbs, leafy greens.

steps.title: A real farmer tends it
steps.description: Our on-the-ground farmer handles everything. You choose the crop and type. Weekly photo updates show exactly what's happening on your plot.

steps.title: Weekly small deliveries
steps.description: As your crop ripens, you receive a small delivery each week — 1–2 kg at a time. No storage problem. No waste. Just fresh food on schedule.

steps.title: Reinvest & grow
steps.description: At the end of each season, reinvest to expand your plot. Your soil becomes richer over more. Your personal farm grows with every year.

dashboardShowcase.heading: Track every stage of your harvest.
dashboardShowcase.intro: From the moment seeds go in to the day of delivery — you see everything. No guessing, no uncertainty.

health.heading: Food the way it was meant to be.
health.intro: When you know exactly where your food comes from, everything changes.

items.title: No pesticides
items.description: Your plot is tended using traditional methods. No chemical inputs, ever.

items.title: Harvested ripe
items.description: Crops are picked at peak ripeness — not early for transit. The difference in taste is immediate.

items.title: Seasonal variety
items.description: You eat what's actually in season — tomatoes in summer, squash in autumn, greens in spring.

items.title: Full traceability
items.description: You know the plot number, the region, the farmer, and the harvest date for everything you eat.

convenience.heading: Your produce, without the market trip.
convenience.intro: We designed this to fit into your life — not the other way around.

items.title: No market trips
items.description: Your weekly harvest is delivered to your door. You never have to rearrange your week around shopping.

items.title: Predictable deliveries
items.description: You know exactly what's coming and when. Plan your meals ahead — no surprises.

items.title: Adjust or pause
items.description: Going on holiday? Pause deliveries. Need less this week? Adjust quantity. You're in control.

items.title: Grows with you
items.description: Pick the share size that fits you. Adjust it at the end of each season — add crops, change your allocation.

progress.heading: A plot that grows with you.
progress.intro: This isn't a subscription you forget about. It's a living piece of land that gets better every year.

farmer.name: Aram Mkrtchyan
farmer.quote: Every plot I tend, I treat like my own family's land.
farmer.bio: Aram has been farming the Armavir valley for 18 years. He grew up watching his father work the same soil. Today he tends over 40 individual plots for families across Yerevan — keeping detailed notes on each one, adjusting for the season, and treating every harvest with care.

seasonal.heading: A full year of harvest.
seasonal.intro: Each season brings different crops. Here's what you can expect across the year.

trust.heading: We're in pre-pilot. Here's exactly what that means.
trust.intro: We believe you deserve the full picture before you sign up.

points.title: Limited to 30 places
points.description: We're starting small intentionally. The first 30 participants will shape how this works for everyone who comes after.

points.title: Launching Spring 2027
points.description: The first harvest season begins in Spring 2027. You'll receive updates as we get closer.

points.title: One region first
points.description: We're starting in Armavir, where our farmer partner is based. More regions come in year two.

points.title: Your input shapes the product
points.description: Pre-pilot members are invited to regular calls with the founder. Your feedback directly influences what we build.

items.question: Do I need farming experience?
items.answer: None at all. The farmer handles all planting, watering, and harvesting. Your role is to enjoy what grows on your plot.

items.question: What does 1 sqm mean here?
items.answer: 1 sqm is your personal share in this farm's annual organic production. At season start, you allocate it across the crops you want, and the farm grows your share accordingly. Through the year, you follow how your share grows.

items.question: What if I don't like a particular vegetable?
items.answer: During sign-up you'll specify preferences and any vegetables you'd like to avoid. The farmer works within those parameters.

items.question: Can I visit my plot?
items.answer: In Year 2 and beyond, plot visits are part of the programme. During the pre-pilot phase, you'll receive photos and updates via your dashboard.

items.question: What happens in winter?
items.answer: The growing season in Armavir runs March through November. During winter months, plots rest and we send preserved goods where possible.

items.question: Is my share really mine?
items.answer: The land itself belongs to the farm partner. What you receive is a personal share in this farm's annual harvest — the produce tied to your share comes to you, along with a real, ongoing relationship with the farm.

about.name: Aleksandr Melikyan
about.paragraph1: I started in code. Eleven years building websites and platforms — readable, functional, clean. I thought in systems and logic. Then I started hiking. Not once or twice — seriously, repeatedly, deep into Armenian mountains through the Bardzunk movement I co-founded. And somewhere on those trails something shifted.
about.paragraph2: I started understanding Armenia differently. Not as a concept or a heritage word, but as soil, altitude, water, light. I started noticing that every Armenian I met — regardless of where they were born or how far they'd drifted — had this pull toward land. Not metaphorical. Physical. Like something encoded.
about.paragraph3:
That's where this idea came from. Not from a business model. From a hike. From watching someone touch Armenian soil and go quiet.

I'm a builder. I know how to start something small, prove it works, and grow it carefully. I've done it with code, with hiking programs, with educational projects. I'm not asking you to trust a pitch — I'm asking you to watch me build this in public, one season at a time. The failures will be documented the same as the successes.
